title: Edge-Transition Optimized Stack with Asymmetric Layer Pairing
scientific_hypothesis: An asymmetric stack with more TiO2 layers than SiO2 layers, optimized for the 650-700 nm transition region, will reduce crosstalk better than symmetric quarter-wave stacks because the edge sharpness depends on index contrast distribution.
design_principle: Dichroic edge filters benefit from asymmetric index profiles that steepen the transition. Placing more high-index layers near the transition region can sharpen the edge. This tests whether layer asymmetry improves band isolation.
proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 | SiO2 | TiO2 - 22 layers total with asymmetric TiO2/SiO2 ratio
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 22 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Asymmetric stack may require more careful process control
TiO2-rich design may have higher stress
known_risks: Asymmetric stacks may be more sensitive to thickness errors
May not converge as reliably as symmetric initialization
Polarization effects at 45° may be exacerbated
execution_request_english: Optimize a 22-layer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate at 45° incidence. Stack sequence: TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke), SiO2 (Gao), TiO2 (Siefke) (22 layers total, starting with TiO2 (Siefke) adjacent to air, with extra TiO2 (Siefke) layers for asymmetry). Materials: TiO2 (Siefke) and SiO2 (Gao) from catalogue. Substrate: SiO2 (Gao) (fused silica). Incident medium: air. Wavelength bands: 450-650 nm (target high reflectance), 700-1000 nm (target high transmittance). Angle: 45 degrees. Design variables: all 22 layer thicknesses in nanometers. Initialize thicknesses with emphasis on transition region layers, then optimize all thicknesses. Maximum 24 layers constraint is satisfied.
